sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A very small creeping moss, with irregular shoots about 1–2 cm long. Its leaves are typically 0.5–1 mm; curved cylindrical capsules, up to about 2 mm long, are borne on long, often reddish setae. It forms mats on living or dead wood, tree bases and roots, soil and stone, usually in moist or sheltered places. Reliable identification may require microscopic examination.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: The sources consulted do not establish food use or toxicity.
